title: POC model selection — Boreal Health systems scoping call

Customer to provide de-identified sample clinical notes and desired label set (by 2025-07-25)
Schedule infra call to discuss VPC/private deployment constraints (pick time next week)
Share security pack (SOC2 + network diagram) with Marta
action_items: Alex Chen: Email benchmark harness link and instructions; due 2025-07-24

transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-07-22 14:00 PST / Duration: ~58 minutes / Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood), Dr. Elena Morales (Boreal), Rajiv Singh (Boreal), Marta Kovac (Boreal), Liam O'Rourke (Boreal)

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. This is Alex from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account, we'll keep this pretty practical — goal today is to lock the POC success criteria, sizing, and the short list of open models we should evaluate. Priya will cover the benchmarks and infra assumptions.

[00:18] Dr. Elena Morales: Hi, thanks. Quick recap from our side — Boreal's use case is clinical summarization + structured extraction from outpatient visit notes across English and Spanish. We care about fidelity to the record, minimal hallucination, and fast enough to be used in a clinician workflow — ideally under 700ms median latency for single-note summarize in our portal.

[00:35] Priya Nair: Helpful, thank you. A couple quick qualification q's before we jump into models — average note length? token distribution? and peak concurrency?

[00:45] Rajiv Singh: Average note is about 1,200 tokens after de-identification, some longer ones to 3k tokens. Traffic profile is spiky — steady 5 rps but peaks of 40-50 rps during shift change. For the POC we'll probably size to replicate peak/steady then measure scaling.

[01:10] Alex Chen: Great. On success criteria, customers we've seen use a mix of objective and subjective metrics. Proposed POC success criteria for Boreal: (1) clinical accuracy — >= 92% on a curated label set (we'll define labels), (2) hallucination rate under 3% as measured by our checklist, (3) median latency <= 800ms for the single-note summarize path at expected batch sizes, (4) operational: ability to run inside your VPC (Private control plane) or Redwood Dedicated, and (5) cost target — token cost per summary under $0.03 equivalent (open model, quantized). Does that align?

[01:45] Dr. Elena Morales: The clinical accuracy number feels right as a starting point, but we need to make sure the label set includes critical safety facts — allergies, meds, problem list. Also any hallucination that invents medications is a showstopper.

[02:05] Marta Kovac: On the security side — we'll need SOC2 docs, an explicit KMS integration story, and audit logs for the POC. Can Redwood support customer-managed keys if we go private?

[02:18] Priya Nair: Yes, for Redwood Private we support customer-managed KMS in the VPC pattern. For the hosted POC we can also use envelope encryption but we should plan for a Private trial if you require keys under your control. We'll include the network diagram in the security pack.

[02:40] Liam O'Rourke: Timeline — what's realistic? We want results to present to execs the second week of September.

[02:48] Alex Chen: If we start next week, typical cadence: 1 week to align prompt sets and ingest sample data, 2 weeks for model evaluation and benchmarking, and then a 4–6 week pilot with 2–3 endpoint configs. So a September meeting is reasonable.

[03:05] Priya Nair: Now on model selection — because you emphasized clinical fidelity and bilingual support, my recommended shortlist of open models to evaluate for the POC:

[03:12] Priya Nair: - Llama 3 13B (llama3-13b) — strong for instruction following; cost-effective, but watch tokenization edge cases for Spanish clinical abbreviations.

[03:25] Priya Nair: - Mistral Large 7B / Mistral 7B Instruct — high quality per-token, good latency at 4-bit quant; sometimes requires careful prompt engineering on medical phrasing.

[03:40] Priya Nair: - Falcon 40B Instruct — higher quality generative/long-form; heavier but we can run quantized 8-bit or 4-bit and see tradeoffs.

[03:50] Priya Nair: - MPT-30B-Instruct or Mosaic MPT variants if we need long-context and structured outputs.

[03:58] Priya Nair: - A domain-adapted Llama3 or an instruction-tuned Llama variant (if we need to fine-tune; Redwood supports light weight LoRA-type fine-tuning during the pilot).

[04:10] Dr. Elena Morales: Are you thinking we'll need to fine-tune on our clinical notes? Or will instruction-tuning + prompt engineering be sufficient?

[04:18] Priya Nair: Good Q. For extraction of discrete fields (meds, allergies) we often see instruction-tuned models with targeted few-shot prompts + validation have decent recall/precision. But for the highest-fidelity production path, a light supervised fine-tune on 1–2k annotated examples gives measurable lifts — especially on domain-specific shorthand. For budget reasons, two parallel tracks are possible: run the zero/few-shot route across the shortlist first, then pick top 1–2 models for a small fine-tune.

[04:48] Alex Chen: One more axis is quantization. 4-bit quantized models reduce cost and GPU memory but can change calibration and increase hallucinations in some models. We'll include quantization-aware evaluation.

[05:05] Rajiv Singh: Regarding latency — you mentioned 800ms median. That seems aggressive for 1.2k tokens on large models. How realistic is that on our Dedicated pool?

[05:18] Priya Nair: For Llama3-13B or Mistral-7B with optimized kernels and batching set properly, sub-second medians are realistic on modern A100/H100 setups for single-request paths. Falcon-40B likely higher latency unless we use sequence-optimized kernel and token caching. We'll capture tail percentiles in the benchmark.

[05:40] Samir Patel: We'll design three benchmark scenarios: 1) single-note interactive summarize (1 user, low-latency), 2) batched throughput for offline summarization (high-throughput), 3) multilingual switch stress test (50/50 English-Spanish). Each scenario will have pass/fail thresholds for latency, accuracy, and economic cost.

[06:05] Dr. Elena Morales: How will you measure hallucination rate? We need a reproducible check so the execs trust results.

[06:12] Priya Nair: We'll use a two-stage approach: automated heuristics to flag invented entities (med names not in the note), followed by manual adjudication on a holdout set of 500 notes. We'll produce precision/recall and a separate hallucination metric: percent of summaries with an invented medication or allergy.

[06:30] Liam O'Rourke: Multilingual coverage — Spanish clinical text has a lot of Spanglish and shorthand. Any model that performs poorly on Spanish we can rule out quickly?

[06:38] Priya Nair: Yes. We'll include a 300-sample Spanish subtest with common shorthand and evaluate. Historically Llama3 variants and some Mistral configs do well with Spanish with prompt tuning; Falcon has mixed results depending on instruction-tune. We should add a 'localization score' to the rubric.

[06:55] Marta Kovac: A couple more compliance asks: can Redwood's auditing show per-request tokens and provide immutable logs? Also data retention policies for POC?

[07:04] Alex Chen: Yes — Redwood Console exposes token-level billing, per-route logs, and we can produce audit export. For POC we'll set a 30-day retention by default but can adjust per contract. We'll send the SOC2, network diagram, and KMS notes in the security pack.

[07:22] Rajiv Singh: For infra, do we need specialized GPUs for 4-bit quant at scale, or can we run on general-purpose instances?

[07:30] Priya Nair: 4-bit quant is supported on both A100 and H100; A100s are fine for the pilot. If you want best latency/tail, H100 with kernel-level optimizations helps for the larger models. We'll propose two capacity profiles in the sizing doc.

[07:45] Alex Chen: Now I'll read the proposed POC plan out loud so we agree on milestones: Week 0 (kickoff + data ingestion + prompts), Week 1–2 (benchmarking across the 4–5 shortlisted models, zero/few-shot + quant configs), Week 3–6 (pilot on 1–2 chosen models including optional fine-tune and infra testing), Week 7–8 (wrap, handoff, runbook + exec summary). Any objection?

[08:08] Dr. Elena Morales: That sounds fine. We want a clear go/no-go gate after week 2 based on the accuracy + hallucination thresholds.

[08:18] Priya Nair: Understood. We'll use the go/no-go that Alex read. We'll also surface cost-per-summary estimates and a recommended serving configuration for integration with your portal (sync vs async).

[08:30] Liam O'Rourke: For integration, our product team prefers an async webhook flow for long notes, and a sync low-latency call for the in-UI highlight. We should test both.

[08:42] Samir Patel: Noted. Benchmarks will include both sync (single request latency) and async throughput (batching) metrics. We'll also include a test for cache/prefix reuse to measure how much KV caching helps on repeated templates.

[09:00] Rajiv Singh: Any concerns about tokenization differences across models breaking our regex-based post-processing?

[09:06] Priya Nair: Good one. We'll include tokenization artifacts in the evaluation matrix and surface if model splits abbreviations inconsistently. If so, we'll add a normalization pass before post-processing or choose a model whose tokenizer aligns better with clinical shorthand.

[09:20] Dr. Elena Morales: Can Redwood help with a small annotation effort? We can probably spare clinician time for 1,000 annotated notes if you provide the tooling.

[09:28] Alex Chen: Yes — Redwood can run the annotation workflow and host the annotation UI for the pilot. We'll include an estimate of clinician hours in the POC proposal.

[09:38] Marta Kovac: Quick question about data residency: our PHI must remain in the US region; is that supported for Redwood Dedicated/Private?

[09:45] Priya Nair: Yes, we can pin capacity to a US-region private deployment. For hosted you can choose region; for strict residency you'll want Redwood Private in your VPC. We'll document options.

[09:58] Alex Chen: Okay, final few items: recommended model shortlist (finalized): Llama3-13B, Mistral-7B-Instruct, Falcon-40B-Instruct, MPT-30B-Instruct (long-context candidate). We'll run the zero/few-shot + 4-bit + 8-bit configs where applicable. We'll surface a recommended two-model pilot after the initial benchmarks.

[10:18] Dr. Elena Morales: If fine-tuning is required, do you have a ballpark for data and time?

[10:24] Priya Nair: For a light supervised fine-tune: 1–2k labeled examples, 48–72 hours training time on a dedicated instance for 13B-class models; more for 30–40B models. We'll include cost estimates in the proposal.

[10:36] Alex Chen: Thanks — we'll send the benchmark harness (link) and a short template for the label schema after this call. Next sync: propose July 29 to review the sample data and agree prompts.

[10:52] Liam O'Rourke: July 29 works.

[11:00] Alex Chen: Great. I'll close with an on-record recap: success criteria (>=92% label accuracy, hallucination <3%, median latency <=800ms), workload sizing (avg 1.2k tokens, peak 50 rps), model shortlist (Llama3-13B, Mistral7B, Falcon-40B, MPT-30B), two-track approach (zero/few-shot then fine-tune if needed), security needs (KMS, SOC2, audit logs), and next steps are the benchmark harness, sample data, and scheduling infra call.

[11:25] Dr. Elena Morales: Thanks, that recap looks good. We'll get the de-identified notes over to Rajiv for export and confirm the July 29rd meeting.

[11:35] Alex Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with documents and links.

End of transcript.
